title: The Unadulterated Influence
chinese: 太上，下知有之，其次，亲而誉之，其次，畏之，其次，侮之。
悠兮其贵言，功成事遂，百姓皆谓：我自然。
pinyin: Tài shàng， xià zhī yǒu zhī， qí cì， qīn ér yù zhī， qí cì， wèi zhī， qí cì， wǔ zhī。
Xìn bù zú yān， yǒu bù xìn yān。
Yōu xī qí guì yán， gōng chéng shì suì， bǎi xìng jiē wèi： wǒ zì rán。
english: In the highest antiquity, (the people) did not know that there were (their rulers). In the next age they loved them and praised them. In the next they feared them; in the next they despised them. Thus it was that when faith (in the Tao) was deficient (in the rulers) a want of faith in them ensued (in the people).

How irresolute did those (earliest rulers) appear, showing (by their reticence) the importance which they set upon their words! Their work was done and their undertakings were successful, while the people all said, “We are as we are, of ourselves!”
